metadata.title: Finding the contextual impacts on Students’ Mathematical performance using a Machine Learning-based Approach

design_fields.q1_rationale: The study does not use TIMSS plausible-value achievement scores as outcomes; instead, it creates a binary benchmark-based outcome from TIMSS PV-derived achievement levels.
design_fields.q2_rationale: Matching text-readable full PDF has no explicit statement that ILSA sampling weights were omitted; weight references concern model parameters, outcome scaling, data variables or class/pixel weighting, not demonstrated sample-weight use.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study uses machine learning methods without mentioning any multilevel modeling or consideration of school clustering in the analysis.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The study does not mention any external validation strategies and appears to rely solely on internal validation methods.
design_fields._pdf_matched: 19. Khoudi et al. (2024). Finding the contextual impacts on Students’ Mathematical performance using a Machine Learning-based Approach.pdf
design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): “This research investigates the potential causes of Moroccan eighth-graders poor mathematical performance in TIMSS 2019… we look into characteristics… that have a high significance in predicting the mathematics test results of Moroccan college students.”
design_fields._q2_audit: Source checked; original extraction rationale: The study explicitly states that it did not apply sampling weights in the analysis.
